facts.statement: Brachypterygius is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from the Late Jurassic of England.
facts.quote: Brachypterygius (meaning ″short wing/paddle″ in Greek) is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from the Late Jurassic of England.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Friedrich von Huene in 1922 because of the short and wide forepaddle.
facts.quote: Brachypterygius was named by Huene in 1922 for the width and shortness of the forepaddle

facts.statement: This medium-sized ichthyosaur had a skull measuring 0.5 to 1.2 meters and a body length up to 4 meters.
facts.quote: Brachypterygius is a medium-sized ichthyosaur, with a skull length of 0.5 - 1.2 m and a body length up to 4 m.

facts.statement: The forepaddle likely possessed five or six digits, with a maximum phalangeal count between 8 and 16.
facts.quote: The forepaddle may have five or six digits, with the maximum phalangeal count being between 8 and 16.

facts.statement: While the holotype was originally thought to come from the Lias Group of Bath, evidence suggests it likely originated from the Kimmeridgian Kimmeridge Clay of Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset.
facts.quote: The holotype of B. extremus was originally thought to be from the Lias Group of Bath, United Kingdom, but other specimens suggest it more likely came from the Kimmeridgian Kimmeridge Clay (Late Jurassic) of Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset, UK.

facts.statement: In 1840, Owen erected Ichthyosaurus trigonus based on a single dorsal vertebra found in the Kimmeridge Clay of Westbrook, Wiltshire.
facts.quote: Owen (1840) erected Ichthyosaurus trigonus based upon a single dorsal vertebra (ANSP 10124) from the Kimmeridge Clay of Westbrook, Wiltshire, UK.

facts.statement: McGowan named the species Grendelius mordax in 1976 based on a large skull discovered in the Kimmeridge Clay of Stowbridge, Norfolk.
facts.quote: A large skull was discovered in the Kimmeridge Clay of Stowbridge, Norfolk, UK and named as a new genus and species, Grendelius mordax, by McGowan in 1976.

facts.statement: Efimov named the genus Otschevia pseudoscythia in 1998 based on a single holotype specimen from the Upper Tithonian of Ulyanovsk in the Volga region of Russia.
facts.quote: Efimov en 1998 nombró a un nuevo género de ictiosaurio, Otschevia pseudoscythia sobre la base de un único espécimen (el holotipo) de la zona de Pseudoscythia (finales del Titoniense en el Jurásico Superior) en Ulyanovsk, en la región del Volga, Rusia.

facts.statement: Maisch and Matzke considered two Russian species to be synonyms in 2000 and referred them to the new combination Brachypterygius pseudoscythius.
facts.quote: Maisch & Matzke, en 2000 consideraron a ambas especies rusas sinónimas la una de la otra, y las refirieron a la nueva combinación B. pseudoscythius.

facts.statement: Brachypterygius lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Brachypterygius es un género de ictiosaurio, miembro de la familia de los oftalmosáuridos,que vivió a finales del período Jurásico.

facts.statement: Fossils of Brachypterygius have been found in England and European Russia.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles han sido hallados en Inglaterra y la Rusia europea.

facts.statement: Brachypterygius lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Brachypterygius is closely related to the genera Platypterygius and Caypullisaurus.
facts.quote: Brachypterygius is closely related to Platypterygius and Caypullisaurus.

facts.statement: A 2015 study by Zverkov and colleagues argued that Grendelius mordax is distinct enough from Brachypterygius extremus to warrant classification as a separate genus and species.
facts.quote: However, a 2015 publication by Zverkov and colleagues instead found Grendelius mordax to be sufficiently different from Brachypterygius extremus to be considered both a separate genus and species.
